title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
steps: 1. Score Odds — Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100. Odds Receipt — press feet.
2. Check Baseline — Find one relevant base rate: how often has this happened in similar situations?
3. Weigh Evidence — Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them. Odds Receipt — camera check.
4. Revise Odds — Issue a revised number and date it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm. Odds Receipt — next action.

title: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
goal: Authority often hides inside delivery.
steps: 1. Read Wrong — Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo. Bad Voice — widen gaze.
2. Keep Words — Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence. Bad Voice — allow opposite.
3. Replay — Then replay it in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order. Bad Voice — next action.

title: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
goal: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
steps: 1. Project — Project the sentence on an inner screen. Edit Font — press feet.
2. Shrink — Shrink it to caption size.
3. Move Metres — Move it two metres away. Edit Font — allow opposite.
4. Lower Opacity — Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
5. Read Version — Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby. Edit Font — next action.

title: RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL
goal: Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.
steps: 1. State Off — State what moved off course in plain language. Return Without — widen gaze.
2. Delete — Delete every adjective about your character.
3. Name Value — Name the value still available and take its nearest next action. Return Without — split duty.
4. Move Whether — Only after moving, decide whether the plan needs repair.
5. Skip Verdict — Skip Verdict verdict is required for re-entry. Return Without — next action.

goal: Reality has already entered the Hold in your mind.
steps: 1. State Fact — State the fact in plain past or present tense. Drop Appeal — feel support.

3. Add Nothing — Refusing its existence adds nothing.’ Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists. Drop Appeal — next action.

steps: 1. Choose Genuinely — Choose one genuinely reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action. Put Good — press feet.

3. Details — While it happens, notice three details worth encoding. Put Good — name feeling.
4. Afterward — Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’. Put Good — next action.

title: BORROW THE SENSATION
goal: Teach the body that a safe signal is not worst-case story.
steps: 1. Select Medically — Select a medically safe exercise that creates a mild feared sensation—brief spinning, stair walking, or breathing through a narrow straw only when appropriate. Borrow Sensation — soften shoulders.

2. Test Sensation — Predict what will happen, induce the sensation briefly, and observe recovery without usual calming it. Test Sensation next. Borrow Sensation — name sensation. Borrow Sensation — next action.

title: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
goal: Some experience forms before it can be explained.
steps: 1. Bring Mind — Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis. Wait Whole — breathe naturally.
2. Ask Body — Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
3. Check Whether — Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift. Wait Whole — name sensation.
4. Leave It Raw — Leave the answer unpolished. Wait Whole — next action.

title: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
goal: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
steps: 1. Small — Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no. Complete Defence — move slowly.
2. Let Unfold — In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop Completion — Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture. Complete Defence — name feeling.
4. Observe Whether — Observe whether the body receives an ending. Complete Defence — next action.

2. Breath — Notice breath, posture, urge, and clarity at each point.
3. Body — Notice where the body can stay present and communicate. Find Body — name feeling.
4. Distance — That distance is data, not a permanent verdict. Find Body — next action.

title: CATCH THE RECOVERY SIGNAL
goal: Settling deserves as much attention as alarm.
steps: 1. Watch Swallow — After body alarm, watch for a swallow, sigh, warmth, trembling, yawn, moisture in the eyes, breath shift, or muscle release. Catch Recovery — hear sound.
2. Name Accurately — When one appears, name it accurately and stay with its after-effect.
3. No Extra Trigger — Do not provoke more. Catch Recovery — name sensation.
4. Look Like — Teach the mind what recovery looks like. Catch Recovery — next action.

title: CLOSE THE BODY FILE
goal: Do not end processing while residue is still asking for attention.
steps: 1. Scan Head — Scan from head to feet for remaining body alarm. Close Body — widen gaze.
2. Select Strongest — Select the strongest residue and give it one stabilising response: support, movement, warmth, grounding in the present, or rest.
3. Rescan — Rescan only once. Close Body — name sensation.
4. State Today — State what is complete today and what belongs to later care. Close Body — next action.

title: FIND THE BUSY HALF
goal: Not every unsettled breath needs a longer exhale.
steps: 1. Observe Ordinary — Observe three ordinary cycles. Find Busy — move slowly.
2. Rate Inhale — Rate inhale effort and exhale release separately.
3. Phase — Which phase is working too hard?. Find Busy — find evidence.
4. Leave Timing — Ease only that side toward neutral—less pulling in or less pushing out—while leaving timing alone.
5. Check Whether — Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases. Find Busy — next action.

title: ALTERNATE THE AIRWAY
goal: Move attention left and right until state feels organised.
steps: 1. Sit Easy — Sit Easy Easy comfortably. Alternate Airway — soften shoulders.

4. Keep Breath — Keep the breath quiet and abandon retention.
5. Finish Nostrils — Finish with both nostrils open. Alternate Airway — next action.

4. Listen Silence — Listen to the silence after the hum, then decide whether another round would still feel kind. Vibration Way — next action.

2. Return Unfilled — When the mind manufactures shapes or stories, recognise image production and return to the unfilled field. Let Darkness — notice detail.
3. Stay Briefly — Stay briefly, then reintroduce light on purpose. Let Darkness — next action.

title: BEFORE THE SENTENCE
goal: Look for thought at the moment of assembly.
steps: 1. Hold Attention — Hold attention quietly and wait. Before Sentence — soften shoulders.
2. Earliest — When a thought begins, notice its earliest form: pressure, fragment, image, word, or felt orientation in space.
3. No Backtracking — Do not chase backward after it fully forms. Before Sentence — notice detail.
4. Birth — Simply Notice ‘birth’ and let the completed thought continue. Before Sentence — next action.

title: FOLLOW IT TO ZERO
goal: A thought’s disappearance is usually ignored.
steps: 1. Select Naturally — Select one naturally occurring thought. Follow Zero — hear sound.
2. Stay Wording — Stay with its exact wording or image as it alters, fragments, loses relevance, or is replaced.
3. Identify Instant — Spot the first instant when no trace can be found. Follow Zero — allow opposite.
4. Let It End — Do not resurrect it to verify the ending. Follow Zero — next action.

4. Perform — Then perform the first with full care. Return Outcome — next action.

title: TRACE THE FIRST SPARK
goal: Find what started the fluctuation before content took over.
steps: 1. Take Recurring — Take one recurring state and move backward through its chain: current thought, preceding sensation, image, memory, external cue, and hidden tendency. Trace First — press feet.
2. Stop Earliest — Stop at the earliest condition you can genuinely spot. Trace First — name feeling.
3. Future — Notice the point where future interruption could happen. Trace First — next action.

title: NOT THIS, STILL HERE
goal: Remove identities without attacking experience.
steps: 1. Body — Notice body, sensation, thought, emotion, and role in turn. Still Here — breathe naturally.
2. Keep Perspective — For each say, ‘Observed—therefore not the whole observer.’ Do not claim they are unreal. Still Here — name sensation.
3. Rest Unlabelled — After the sequence, rest with what remains unlabelled, then reconnect to name and place. Still Here — next action.

title: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
goal: A pattern is less inevitable once you find where it already failed to appear.
steps: 1. Name Pattern — Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response. Find Where — hear sound.
2. Find Misses — Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare Conditions — Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care. Find Where — notice detail.
4. Transplant Edge — Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like. Find Where — next action.

title: RUN THE START GATE TWICE
goal: The first start can be rehearsal; the second one becomes real.
steps: 1. Stage Door — Choose the opening movements: open the file, place the tool, find the line, or position your hands. Keep it under ten seconds. Run Start — loosen hands.
2. Dry Launch — Perform that sequence once without producing work. Stop at the edge of action; this is the dry launch.
3. Full Reset — Return your hands or screen to neutral exactly once. Leave the plan unchanged or add another rehearsal. Run Start — pick action.
4. Live Entry — Repeat the same sequence and continue straight into thirty seconds of real work. Run Start — next action.

title: DIFFERENCE INSIDE ONE FIELD
goal: Diversity need not become division.
steps: 1. Contrasting — Notice two contrasting experiences—pleasant and painful, self and other, sound and silence. Difference Inside — widen gaze.
2. Hold Distinct — Hold their distinct qualities without merging them.
3. Include Shared — Then include the shared field in which both are present. Difference Inside — notice detail.
4. Let Difference — Let difference remain vivid without translating it into separation. Difference Inside — next action.

title: ROTATE THE CHAIR
goal: One perspective is data, not the whole room.
steps: 1. Describe Event — Describe the event from your position. Rotate Chair — feel support.

3. Watch Behaviour — Stand as a neutral observer and Keep behaviour only. Rotate Chair — split forecast.
4. Ask Future — Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next. Rotate Chair — next action.

title: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
goal: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
steps: 1. Say Alarm — Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven phrasing or fewer. Move Heaviest — feel support.
2. Shift Stress — Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Find Weight — Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word. Move Heaviest — notice detail.
4. Keep Signal — Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence. Move Heaviest — next action.

title: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
goal: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.

title: TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON
goal: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
steps: 1. Ask Far — Ask how far ahead consequences can meaningfully alter today’s move: tonight, one week, six months. Today Furthest — feel support.
2. Imagine Line — Imagine a line at that horizon.
3. Park Scenario — Park every scenario beyond it unless it changes a present safety or commitment fact. Today Furthest — pick action.
4. Decide Information — Decide using information inside the line. Today Furthest — next action.

3. Ask Strengthens — Ask what starts, strengthens, interrupts, and ends that process. Turn Label — next action.

title: MEANING ON HOLD

steps: 1. Hold Event — Hold the event without explaining it. Meaning Hold — hear sound.

3. Name Meaning — Until all three exist, Name every meaning temporary. Meaning Hold — notice detail.
4. Assign Narrowest — Then assign the narrowest meaning supported. Meaning Hold — next action.

title: ONE WORD, ONE BREATH, RELEASE
goal: Compress the noise without pretending it is solved.
steps: 1. Choose Temporary — Choose a temporary word that holds the issue: betrayal, pressure, uncertainty, loss. Word Breath — press feet.
2. Say During — Say it once during a natural breath, feel its weight, and let the word leave with the breath’s end. Word Breath — allow opposite.
3. Keep One Name — Do not replace it with a second Name for thirty seconds. Word Breath — next action.

title: GIVE THE FORECAST EDGES
goal: A vague fear cannot lose because it never defines a result.
steps: 1. Sharpen Forecast — Sharpen the prediction with who, what visible event, exact time window, location, and clear threshold. Give Forecast — widen gaze.
2. Define — Define the sign of the event not happening. Give Forecast — notice detail.
3. Set Review — Set a review date and refuse to score the forecast before then. Give Forecast — next action.

title: TURN DOWN THE DOMINANT CHANNEL
goal: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.
steps: 1. Identify Loudest — Spot the loudest recall channel—image, sound, touch, smell. Turn Down — loosen hands.
2. Reduce Brightness — Reduce its brightness, volume, proximity, or texture slightly. Turn Down — estimate odds.
3. Date Clothing — At the identical time strengthen neutral context such as room layout, date, clothing, or distant sound. Turn Down — next action.

3. Deliver Limit — Deliver the exact limit you planned—no extra smile, apology, or attack. Soft Jaw — split duty.
4. Let Articulation — Let articulation stay clear while muscular threat signalling drops. Soft Jaw — next action.

title: THE POINT OF NO MORE INFLUENCE
goal: The body needs to know when available action is complete.
steps: 1. Remain Unknown — Name what you have already done, what remains unknown, and which outcomes no longer respond to effort. Point No — press feet.
2. Boundary — Notice the exact boundary where influence ends. Point No — allow opposite.
3. Use Physical — Use one physical closing action and redirect into a present responsibility. Point No — next action.

title: CHANGE THE MENTAL TOOL, NOT THE PRESSURE
goal: Wrong mental mode makes effort repeat itself.
steps: 1. Decide Accept — Classify the demand as SOLVE, DECIDE, FEEL, ACCEPT, COMMUNICATE, or WAIT. Change Mental — widen gaze.
2. Name Mode — Name the mode currently running. Change Mental — pick action.
